Where the write-up was silent, B resolved each gap toward the engineer's process rather than domain practice. It took excess to mean cutting to exactly the limit with a cascade, read 'one snapshot' as simultaneous apply, and allowed at most one flip per cycle. It applied the strict '>38' boundary even though '38' is called a 'target'. Of B's 8 flags, 4 match real losses (exact cut to the limit, cascade, snapshot simultaneity, one flip per cycle). domainPull: The pull is strongest around WIP limits and closures. In Kanban a WIP limit blocks intake, but here 'Limits don't bite yet' lets tickets land over the limit and then pushes the excess downstream. A ROUTINE team's ordinary work ('closes a quarter of its tickets') is counted as LOST, in the same tally as 'closed-without-action' overflow and the backlog cut, whereas domain sense would count those closures as throughput. Two further traps sit in the same language. ESCALATED teams 'bounce half... to the team upstream', against the usual direction of escalation. 'The board target is 38' invites reading 38 as a goal or treating reaching it as a breach, when the rule is strictly over 38, and that boundary decides cycle 5 (total exactly 38, no cut). No operator who produced work fell for any of these. B explicitly applied 'strictly over 38'.
preReadNamedTheBreak: n/a: nobody fell. B was exact, A returned null with no working, and C's pre-read notes read 'Not provided. The earlier response was stopped by a safety classifier.', so they name nothing.
preReadEffect: No difference that can be measured. C's whole output, pre-read notes included, was lost to a stop it attributes to a safety classifier, so there are no pre-read notes, flags (0, against B's 8) or numbers to compare. summary: Only B produced a report, and it matches the true answer exactly; its working checks out independently, and it flagged 4 of the 10 real document losses. A returned nothing, and C returned placeholders after a stop it attributes to a safety classifier, so neither the domain traps nor the pre-read can be tested on them. The biggest document flaw is not a compression: the write-up embeds the full expected Report, which the writer's list omits, so an exact match cannot by itself show the rules were understood.
